explain.say: On a cold Christmas Eve, a small boy is crying among the graves on the Kent marshes when a convict in leg irons grabs him. That is how Charles Dickens opens Great Expectations, published in 1860 and 1861. The panels follow Pip, an orphan who dreams of becoming a gentleman.

explain.say: Here is Pip's web. Joe, the kind blacksmith, raises him. Miss Havisham, jilted on her wedding day, trains Estella to break men's hearts. Now look at the link from Magwitch: the convict Pip once fed is secretly paying for everything. Which link do you think Pip will be most ashamed of?

Look at the third panel. After Estella sneers at his rough hands, Pip feels ashamed of Joe and the forge. Dickens is writing a social novel, a story that shows how class and money shape people. Pip's new money lets him rise, but it also makes him a snob. Can money buy you a better self?

explain.say: Now the twist in the fifth panel. The money never came from Miss Havisham. It came from Magwitch, who was transported to Australia and made a fortune there. Pip's gentility rests on a criminal's love. Why might Dickens want a gentleman's fortune to come from the bottom of society?

explain.say: Dickens wrote two endings. On the left, the first: Pip and Estella meet briefly and part. On the right, the one he published after his friend Edward Bulwer-Lytton objected: they meet in the ruined garden, with a hint they may stay together. Superb work. Challenge: which ending suits a story about lost illusions?

faq.a: Abel Magwitch is the escaped convict Pip helps on the marshes as a child. Transported to Australia, he grows rich and secretly pays for Pip to become a gentleman.
asks: Who is the convict in Great Expectations?

faq.q: Why is Miss Havisham still in her wedding dress?
faq.a: She was jilted on her wedding day, so she stopped every clock at that moment and has worn the dress ever since, with the wedding cake rotting on the table. She raises Estella to take revenge on men.
asks: Why did Miss Havisham stop the clocks?

faq.a: Magwitch, the convict. Pip believes it is Miss Havisham, and she lets him think so, until Magwitch returns illegally from Australia and reveals the truth.
A novel of growing up, following one person from childhood to maturity as they learn who they are. Great Expectations, Jane Eyre and David Copperfield are classic examples.
asks: What is a coming of age novel?

faq.q: Why did Dickens change the ending of Great Expectations?
faq.a: His friend the novelist Edward Bulwer-Lytton thought the original, in which Pip and Estella simply part, was too bleak. Dickens rewrote it so they meet in the ruins of Satis House with a hint of a future together.
asks: What was the original ending of Great Expectations?

facts: Great Expectations was serialised weekly in Dickens's magazine All the Year Round from December 1860 to August 1861.
Dickens rewrote the ending after advice from Edward Bulwer-Lytton.
The novel is narrated in the first person by the adult Pip looking back on his life.
